$comment: PS-6801 HTST milk pasteurizer twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from the pasteurizer data, the PMO and EU 853/2004; the PLC sends only what it measures.

identification.model: Pasteurizer D Base type, market milk, 10,000 l/h, plate heat exchanger with regeneration
identification.description: HTST pasteurizer for market milk: regeneration, hot water heating, holding tube, flow diversion valve, ice water cooling
identification.phe: Plate heat exchanger with regenerative, heating and cooling sections (gasketed plates, AISI 316)
identification.holding: Climbing holding tube, 48.5 mm ID, sized for 15 s at the rated flow
identification.fdd: Flow diversion valve after the holding tube: forward to the regenerator, divert back to the balance tank
identification.timing: Frequency-controlled feed pump with magnetic flow meter and flow control (the PMO calls this a meter based timing system)
identification.booster: Booster pump on the raw side, interlocked so the pasteurized side of the regenerator stays at the higher pressure

process.source: Tetra Pak Pasteurizer D Base product leaflet (2018), market milk, 10,000 l/h version: capacity, temperature program, holding time, regeneration, ice water and steam figures. Normal running flow 9,500 l/h (95 % of the rated capacity), milk density 1.032 kg/l and specific heat 3.93 kJ/kg K: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

legal.source: Grade "A" Pasteurized Milk Ordinance (PMO), Item 16p and Appendix I: HTST 72 °C (161 °F) for 15 s; pasteurized milk in the regenerator at least 6.9 kPa (1 psi) above the raw milk. Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, Annex III, Section IX, Chapter II: at least 72 °C for 15 s. The twin uses 72.0 °C, the stricter of 72 °C and 161 °F (71.7 °C).

holding_tube.source: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, chapter Heat exchangers: V = Q x HT / (3600 x eta), example 10,000 l/h, 15 s, D 48.5 mm, eta 0.85 -> about 26.5 m (this twin uses exactly that example). Upward slope >= 2.1 cm/m: Grade "A" Pasteurized Milk Ordinance (PMO), Item 16p and Appendix I. Temperature loss along the tube 0.2 K: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

regenerator.source: Area sized so that the clean section gives the leaflet's 85 % regeneration at 10,000 l/h (balanced counterflow, eps = NTU / (1 + NTU)). Clean U 4,500 W/m2 K (below the handbook's ~5,000 for thin plates, milk on both sides), U ~ flow^0.6, raw-side pressure drop 0.30 bar at the rated flow: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

heater.source: Clean U about 5,000 W/m2 K and heating medium 2 - 3 °C above the pasteurization temperature: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, chapter Heat exchangers. Area sized for a 3 K approach at 10,000 l/h. Hot water flow 15 m3/h, U ~ milk flow^0.35, milk-side pressure drop 0.60 bar at the rated flow: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

pressures.source: Raw milk pressure at the regenerator inlet and pasteurized milk pressure at the regenerator outlet (gauge), and the 0.3 bar early-warning margin: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file. The 6.9 kPa minimum is the PMO's.

energy.source: Steam 3 bar g: Tetra Pak Pasteurizer D Base product leaflet (2018), market milk, 10,000 l/h version. Latent heat 2,133 kJ/kg at 4 bar absolute (steam tables). Hot water unit efficiency 0.95 and the 1.3 x alert ratio: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

cip.source: Validated production run between two CIPs (the PMO asks for cleaning at least once each day used unless an extended run is accepted), lye return temperature and the start-of-run pressure drop ratio that marks an incomplete clean: assumption: typical value, replace with your pasteurizer data sheet / validation file

demo.note: Demo only: the plant clock runs 60 times faster, so a 10-hour production run with its slow fouling and the CIP that ends it shows in 10 minutes. In the demo the failure modes ramp in over about a minute.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

heater_fouling.name: Protein fouling in the heating section
heater_fouling.symptoms: heating section U falls, the hot water must run hotter (approach grows), milk pressure drop rises

regen_fouling.name: Fouling in the regenerative section
regen_fouling.symptoms: regeneration % falls, approach grows, raw-side pressure drop rises, steam per litre rises

pressure_diff_loss.name: Regenerator pressure differential lost (booster or back-pressure fault)
pressure_diff_loss.symptoms: pasteurized side no longer 6.9 kPa above the raw side: leak risk, the FDD diverts

flow_timing_drift.name: Flow control / timing drift (flow above the sealed capacity)
flow_timing_drift.symptoms: flow above 10,000 l/h, fastest-particle holding time below 15 s

heating_unstable.name: Hot water unit unstable (steam valve hunting, low steam)
heating_unstable.symptoms: holding temperature sags towards 72 °C and swings; the FDD diverts again and again

stlr_drift.name: Recorder-controller (STLR) sensor reads high
stlr_drift.symptoms: STLR above the indicating thermometer: the FDD would let colder milk forward

cip_incomplete.name: Incomplete CIP (lye too cold, residual deposit)
cip_incomplete.symptoms: the run starts with a heating section pressure drop above clean

cip_skipped.name: CIP skipped: run beyond the validated length
cip_skipped.symptoms: hours since CIP beyond the validated run; fouling keeps growing
